beats.narration_en: Why is this road sinking into the sea?
It's a bridge across the Corinth Canal in Greece.
When a ship is coming gates stop the traffic.
Then the whole road sinks about twenty-six feet underwater.
It goes down at about thirteen feet a minute.
And settles almost on the bottom of the canal.
Ships sail right over the top of the drowned road.
With nothing above the water no mast is ever too tall.
A lift bridge would need towers taller than the masts.
Once the ship has passed the road rises again dripping wet.
That's why drivers here sometimes wait for their road to come back up.
